‘inflammatory myopathy’ is an umbrella term for a heterogeneous group of diseases that can be classified into several subgroups based on clinical, morphological, immunological, molecular and genetic features.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
autoantibody profiling has become an important diagnostic tool for inflammatory myopathy.
autoantibodies in inflammatory myopathies are a useful tool for diagnosis and prognosis and may also help to understand the underlying mechanisms.
autoantibodies can be useful for the diagnosis of inflammatory myopathy and that autoantibody profiles can be useful for predicting the prognosis of inflammatory myopathy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
myositis is not a single entity but comprises a spectrum of diseases that can be grouped according to their clinical and morphological features.
autoantibody testing is a valuable diagnostic tool that can provide important clues to the underlying pathogenesis of inflammatory myopathy.
the classification of myopathies should not only consider the clinical phenotype, but also incorporate molecular, morphological and autoantibody data, which are increasingly becoming available.
